statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 9, low, for the 02:00Z hour. Nasdaq-100 futures have faded from the 29,480.25 session high back to 29,310.50, down 77.25 points and 0.26%, at 02:02Z, a second visit to the 29,303.50 low after the earlier recovery to 29,430.25. Both directions of the overnight band have now retraced at least once, which is the opposite of the no-retracement path Tail measures, but price is sitting at a session extreme with a fresh negative tech catalyst, so Tail rises from 7 to 9 rather than easing further. S&P 500 futures are 7,692.00, up 0.01%, inside a 21.75-point band, so the drag is tech-specific rather than index-wide. Stress is 40, moderate, up from 38: Samsung Electronics fell between 5 and 8 percent after a shareholder-return announcement that disappointed, taking the KOSPI down 1.85%, while WTI at $85.46, down 1.84%, and Brent at $92.79, down 1.69%, hold their pre-announcement discount and long-end Treasury yields stay near multi-month highs with the 30-year at 5.23% and the 10-year at 4.69% on the 20 August H.15. Confidence is 86, high, on two independent live futures quotes, a second index verified live, verified Asian cash levels, oil verified from two sources, an official yield release and a calendar cross-checked against two independent feeds. The narrow 18:00Z-20:00Z danger window around the US Treasury news conference on new Iran sanctions is unchanged and Tail remains below the block threshold throughout the forecast.
recommendation: The overnight price path remains two-way, but it has shifted from a completed round trip to a retest of its lower edge. Nasdaq-100 futures printed a high of 29,480.25, sold to 29,303.50, recovered to 29,430.25 and have returned to 29,310.50 at 02:02Z, so both edges of a 177-point band have been visited and both directions have retraced. What has changed is the cause and the location: price sits at a session extreme, and the softness has an identifiable tech-specific source in the Korean session, where Samsung Electronics fell sharply after its shareholder-return announcement disappointed and the KOSPI lost 1.85%. That justifies a small increase in Tail from 7 to 9 without approaching the block threshold, because there is still no shallow-pullback sequence, no repeated extension after a failed retracement and no cross-asset confirmation. S&P 500 futures are flat inside a 21.75-point range, Dow futures are unchanged, delayed Treasury futures are firmer to the tune of 0.02% to 0.34% implying small yield relief, gold is 0.27% higher and VIX closed Friday at 14.89. Latest-session leadership was mixed, with five of eight megacaps higher but semiconductors averaging -0.70%. The exposures that remain are cross-asset and scheduled: long-end yields near multi-month highs, the 18:00Z US Treasury news conference on new Iran sanctions, and Wednesday's PCE, GDP and durable-goods stack at 12:30Z alongside Nvidia results after the close. Those shape Stress and the conditional path; none is observed price-path evidence and none maps to a blocking Tail level at this time.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures retest the 29,303.50 overnight low at 29,310.50, down 0.26%, as Samsung's shareholder-return disappointment drags Korean tech: Tail 9, low, mapped policy state EA_ON, with conditional readings of 8 to 18 across the next twenty-three hours.
body:
Four and a half hours into the Globex week the Nasdaq-100 has traced a complete band and returned to its lower edge. Futures topped at 29,480.25, sold to a session low of 29,303.50, recovered to 29,430.25 at 01:13Z and are 29,310.50, down 77.25 points and 0.26%, at 02:02Z on Yahoo Finance, with Investing.com showing 29,369.50, down 0.06%, at 01:54Z inside a 29,335.00-29,470.25 range. Against the 29,387.75 previous close that is a modest net decline within a band roughly 177 points wide. The structure is still two-way, because both edges have been visited and both directions have retraced, but the second test of the low is a change from the previous hour and price is now at a session extreme.

The drag has an identifiable and largely idiosyncratic source. Samsung Electronics fell between 5 and 8 percent in Seoul after announcing shareholder returns of up to 110 trillion won, about $79.4 billion for the year, which analysts judged smaller and less specific than expected, with no treasury-share cancellation. The KOSPI fell 1.85% to 6,784.82 while SK Hynix rose 0.4%, so even within Korea the weakness was concentrated rather than systemic. Reuters reported the wider Asian session as flat, with the Nikkei near unchanged, Taiwan down 0.5% and MSCI's Asia-Pacific ex-Japan index down 0.2%.

Cross-asset context contradicts a broadening move. S&P 500 futures are 7,692.00, up 0.01%, inside a 7,681.50-7,703.25 band, and delayed context shows Dow futures unchanged, VIX futures 0.3% lower, gold 0.27% higher and two-, five-, ten- and thirty-year Treasury futures 0.02% to 0.34% firmer, which is small overnight yield relief rather than another leg higher in rates. VIX closed Friday at 14.89, down 6.00%. Crude has pared part of its earlier decline: WTI is $85.46, down 1.84%, and Brent $92.79, down 1.69%, after Reuters reported profit-taking ahead of the Treasury announcement and following a second consecutive weekly gain of more than 5%.

The rates backdrop remains the main structural exposure. The 20 August H.15 shows the two-year at 4.19%, the ten-year at 4.69% and the thirty-year at 5.23%, with the long end near multi-month highs. This week brings $69 billion of two-year notes on Tuesday, $70 billion of five-year notes on Wednesday and $44 billion of seven-year notes on Thursday, so a long-end auction tail remains the most plausible route from rates into Nasdaq-100 structure.

Geopolitics is an ongoing, largely priced condition rather than a fresh discontinuity. The Strait of Hormuz remains essentially shut and indirect US-Iran contacts continue. The scheduled step is the 18:00Z Treasury news conference at which the Secretary has threatened the toughest sanctions in history. No new escalation has been verified in the last hour, and falling oil into the headline is a partial pre-discount.

On the calibration that matters, Tail measures the pathological price path that denies mean reversion long enough to overwhelm a reverse or grid approach. A session extreme revisited with a fresh negative sector catalyst is a mild amplifier, while the completed two-way band, the flat broad index and the absence of failed retracements are direct contrary evidence. Tail is therefore 9, low. Stress at 40 carries the Korean tech drag, the scheduled sanctions announcement, elevated long-end yields, heavy coupon supply and Wednesday's PCE and Nvidia stack. Confidence at 86 reflects two independent live futures quotes, a second index verified live, verified Asian cash levels from two sources, an official yield release, oil verified from two sources and a calendar cross-checked against two independent feeds.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past twenty-four hours is nearly complete: twenty hourly assessments are available and four clock-hours are marked unavailable, at 07:00Z, 10:00Z, 11:00Z and 12:00Z on 23 August. Tail held 4 through every hour of the weekend futures halt, when no Nasdaq-100 price path could develop at all, stepped to 15 in the 22:00Z reopen hour to cover the still-unpriced weekend queue, then fell back to 9 at 23:00Z, 8 at 00:00Z and 7 at 01:00Z once the reopen printed without a gap and produced a complete round trip. The mapped policy state stayed EA_ON and the dominant mode remained normal in every available hour, so no hour approached the block threshold. Stress traced a full weekend arc: 36 at the start of the window, a low of 34 through the European morning and early afternoon, then a steady climb across the evening to 45 in the last three pre-reopen hours as the tariff escalation and Monday's scheduled Iran announcement accumulated, before easing to 42, 39 and 38 once the reopen cleared. Confidence sat between 82 and 87 throughout, dipping to its low of 82 in the reopen hour when the first live print was still incomplete and recovering to 86 immediately afterwards.
outlookSummary: The current hour carries Tail 9 and Stress 40 on observed structure: futures have completed a 177-point band and returned to its lower edge at 29,310.50, down 0.26%, with a fresh tech-specific catalyst in Samsung's shareholder-return disappointment and a flat S&P 500 futures contract alongside. Conditional Tail then eases to 8 through the quietest Asian and early European hours, where two-way trade has historically been most reliable and no US release is scheduled, while Stress decays to 38. Tail steps to 9 for the European cash open and holds 9 to 10 through the European morning and the US pre-market build, with the 12:30Z Chicago Fed National Activity Index treated as a medium-impact checkpoint at Tail 10 rather than a step. The US cash open inside the 13:00Z hour carries 15 for opening-auction continuation risk, easing to 14, 12 and 11 across the auction window and the midday lull. The path peaks at 18 with Stress 49 and mode event/whipsaw for the 18:00Z and 19:00Z hours around the US Treasury news conference on new Iran sanctions, covering both the initial repricing and a delayed second leg, then decays to 14 at the 20:00Z cash close, 10 into the futures maintenance break and 8 by Tuesday's Asian session. Every forecast hour maps to EA_ON, because none reaches the block threshold on conditional risk alone. Confidence declines from 86 to 71 across the window purely with forecast distance from the last verified price observation, not because of conflicting evidence.
